task.title: Revamp Smart Dashboard (AI chart creation) page UI with custom CSS
request: Revamp the UI of the Smart Dashboard page — the internal preview surface for
AI chart creation — to be way prettier with custom CSS styling.
The page lives in the `@klaviyo/smart-dashboard-pages` package
(`client/app/smart-dashboard-pages/src/SmartDashboardPage.tsx`). Today it is a
bare stack of component-library primitives (Box, TextArea, SelectBox, Button)
with no visual hierarchy or identity: you paste or load an AnalyticsVizConfig
JSON, click Render, and see the chart previewed at full-page / split-screen /
narrow-chat widths.
Requirements:
- A distinct, polished visual design driven by custom CSS (a dedicated
stylesheet in this package), not just default component-library spacing.
- Clear visual hierarchy: a styled page header, a visually distinct
config-editor panel, and a chart-preview area where the three preview widths
read as labeled preview cards.
- The chart area's empty state and the JSON parse-error banner remain, restyled
to match the new design.
- All existing behavior is unchanged: example-loader dropdown, config text
editor, Render button, error handling, three preview widths, and every
existing `data-testid` stays intact.
- Keep the change scoped to `client/app/smart-dashboard-pages`; do not touch
`SelfFetchingAnalyticsViz` (the chart renderer) — the revamp is the page
chrome around it.
- Update the package's unit tests where styling hooks changed; add focused
tests for any new presentational logic.
Local verification context: the page is served at `/smart-dashboard`, gated by
the `smart_dashboard_enabled` Statsig gate with a
`localStorage['smart-dashboard-otter-access-pass'] = 'true'` staff bypass.
Chart data comes from the local app backend `POST /ajax/smart-dashboard/viz`.
NOTE — this is the fender repo, running in an isolated git worktree (no
direnv/Nix). To run tests/typecheck/lint here you MUST: (1) run
`yarn install` in the worktree first (Yarn PnP); (2) prefix commands with
`CI=true SKIP_DIRENV_NIX_ENFORCEMENT=true` to pass the enforce-direnv-nix
plugin (CI is forwarded by turbo to package scripts; SKIP only covers the
outer call); (3) invoke turbo via `yarn exec turbo` (it's not on PATH under
PnP); (4) scope tests with `--filter=@klaviyo/<package>` — the bare
`turbo test` script is a stub that exits 1. Example:
`CI=true SKIP_DIRENV_NIX_ENFORCEMENT=true yarn exec turbo run test --filter=@klaviyo/smart-dashboard-pages`.
